data.body:
rebar-debug final report — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1419

PROBLEM. The `Git version floor gate` failed every in-flight change branched before its
data file landed, regardless of what the change touched.

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE. The step read `.github/git-version-floor.txt` from the checked-out
patchset tree and `exit 1`-ed on absence, while Gerrit's Verified lane sources the workflow
DEFINITION from the target branch. Confirmed at runtime, not statically.

PROOF. Lifted the step's `run:` script out of the workflow YAML and executed it under bash:
absent-file tree -> exit 1 with `::error::missing`; present-file tree -> exit 0 reporting
'declared floor: git >= 2.38; runner has git 2.55.0'. The runner's git is far above the
floor, so file absence is the sole cause — that splits tree-skew from a genuine under-floor
runner.

TEST. tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py (6 tests). It parses the real step out of
the workflow and runs it against purpose-built trees, so it asserts behavior rather than
wording. Seen RED first (3 skew tests failed; the 3 enforcement tests passed, proving they
were not vacuous). Held out from the fix subagent — moved out of its working tree, not merely
omitted from its prompt. Teeth proven in BOTH directions:
  - re-introducing the exact root cause (restore `::error::` + `exit 1`) returns the 3 skew
    tests to RED;
  - weakening 980d's enforcement to a no-op returns the 3 enforcement tests to RED.

FIX. One step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml, +9/-2. The absent-file branch now
logs '<floorfile> not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping; the gate
re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change' and exits 0. Everything below the guard
— the floor parse, the sort -V comparison, the success line, and the under-floor
`::error::` + `exit 1` — is byte-for-byte unchanged.

AC COVERAGE.
  - AC1: a pre-gate tree passes. Replicated against the REAL tree of c433663721^ (materialised
    with git archive) — the exact .github/ shape change 1416 had, module-size-limit.txt but no
    git-version-floor.txt: exit 0 with the skip line. Proven RED-first.
  - AC2: an under-floor git (stubbed at 2.30.2) still exits non-zero naming required 2.38,
    installed 2.30.2, and 'Upgrade git on the runner image'. tests/conftest.py's
    pytest_configure session-abort and tests/_git_floor.py are untouched.
  - AC3: with the if-present guard the missing-file case is a SKIP, not a failure, so the log
    line — not a failure message — carries the remedy. It names the cause (the tree predates
    the gate) and the resolution (re-enforces on rebase / post-merge) rather than just the
    filename. This is the plan-review E1 advisory's point; the AC's intent (do not send an
    author hunting for a file they never touched) is met by the skip line.
  - AC4: both tree cases verified — three fixtures (no floor file / floor file / floor file
    with an under-floor git shim), plus the real pre-gate tree replication above.

SCOPE & SAFETY. Caller sweep: the gate step is CI-only; the other floor consumers
(tests/_git_floor.py, tests/conftest.py, docs) read the file directly and are unaffected. The
existing pins test_ci_reads_the_floor_from_the_single_source and
test_consumers_declare_the_same_floor both still pass. The change restores behavior rather
than creating any, adds no dependency (PyYAML is already a test dependency), and weakens no
existing test — no pre-existing test file was touched. make lint, make typecheck, actionlint
and zizmor all clean; tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py + test_ci_workflow_parity.py +
test_workflow_names.py all pass (60/60).

SIBLINGS. Construct sweep over every workflow step that reads a repo artifact found nine
further UNGUARDED gate steps in _build-and-test.yml, plus two in gerrit-verify.yaml's
golden-path job. Two are LIVE exposure (scripts added 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-03), confirmed
empirically to exit 2 with 'can't open file' when the script is absent. Filed as
1909-c1a7-9f20-440f (brattish-ladyish-jaguar), linked discovered_from this bug, rather than
expanded into this change beyond its attested one-step blast radius.

RESIDUAL RISK. The ee2a convention currently depends on authors remembering a comment. That
fragility is dispositioned in 1909's AC list as a proposed structural guard — a check that
fails when a Verified-lane step runs a repo artifact without the if-present guard.

STATUS. Change 1419 pushed; awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Not closing until both
are green and the change has merged.
